observations_not_on_main_spine.observation: CLOSES OB-6. The mid-scan six-zero module counters are fully explained and fixed in cycle 4 slot 1. Evidence chain: Scan::new seeds zeros (core/scan/mod.rs) -> run_with_ledger_inner upserts Running with them (core/engine/mod.rs:653-654) -> finalise_scan is the sole writer (core/engine/mod.rs:991-996). Both uploaded debug bundles were status:Running, which is why both showed zeros while their event streams held ~70 module_start / ~60 module_done / ~9 module_error / ~11 module_skipped.

Deliberate design limit recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight: the event stream CANNOT reconstruct the engine's six counters. There is no distinct EventKind for a timeout (it arrives as a plain ModuleError), a cache replay, or a dedup; and ModuleSkipped is not disjoint from ModuleStart — gate-skips are emitted with no preceding start (Engine::emit_module_skipped, core/engine/mod.rs:477-482) while dispatched-then-opted-out modules emit one first (dispatch.rs:548). ModuleEventTally therefore reports event counts under their event names and offers no in-flight figure.

cycle_33_slots.finding: Non-loopback bind had NO authentication — only a startup warn!.

LOOPBACK DEFAULT IS BYTE-IDENTICAL: resolve() returns None, no layer installed, no startup output — proven at runtime.

cycle_33_au046_verified: AU-046 (cluster.rs:245-248) — DEFECT CONFIRMED, NAIVE FIX REFUTED. Do not apply the obvious remedy without reading this. CONFIRMED (two independent adversarial skeptics, high confidence, plus an independent hand trace): the rule joins alias->identifier on `!alias_srcs.is_disjoint(srcs)` over corroborating_sources() — the bare module NAME — while its own docstring (cluster.rs:170-175) and inline comment both promise the identifier is scoped to 'the alias's own account(s)' so that 'a co-author's email, another alias's identifiers, or an unrelated breach-dump stranger can't be fused in'. The code does not deliver that. CONCRETE REACHABLE FALSE POSITIVE: a scan with TWO confirmed aliases (alice, bob) where github_user surfaced an Email for each — both Emails carry source name 'github_user', both are platform-sourced, so alice's alias shares a source with BOTH and bob's email is emitted as a High 'Alias alice resolves to real-world identifier(s)'. That is precisely the case the docstring claims is excluded. REFUTED FIX DIRECTION (verified against module source — do NOT do this): switching the join to corroborating_records() (the (source,summary) key that core::entity::mod.rs:897-917 documents as 'the correct key for co-occurrence') would make AU-046 fire NEVER. The platform modules attach a DIFFERENT summary to the handle than to the identifier it published: github_user mod.rs:180 'GitHub profile @{login}' on the Username vs mod.rs:209 'Twitter handle from GitHub profile @{login}' / :307 'Company from…' / :332 'Location from…' on the derived entities; keybase mod.rs:218 'Keybase profile for {u}' vs :234 'Name from Keybase profile {u}'. Record equality therefore holds for NEITHER the false-positive nor the genuine case, so the rule goes silent — a total false negative traded for a false positive. corroborating_records is the right key for same-breach/same-page co-occurrence (its documented use); it is the WRONG key for 'this module derived B from A's profile', where the modules deliberately vary the summary. OPEN DESIGN DECISION for the next cycle (needs a maintainer call or a corpus, NOT an autonomous semantic change): (a) require the identifier's evidence summary from the shared source to NAME the alias handle — works for github_user and keybase, whose summaries embed the login, but risks silent false negatives for any module whose summary omits it, and substring matching needs word-boundary care even though is_anchorable_handle already screens short/generic handles; (b) STRICTLY-SAFER PARTIAL — drop an identifier only when its evidence positively names a DIFFERENT alias present in the scan; kills the concrete two-alias FP above with zero false-negative risk, but leaves the non-alias co-author case, so the docstring must then be corrected to claim only what is enforced; (c) key on a structured attribute (github_user mod.rs:209 already stamps `github_login`), which is exact but per-module and needs a shared convention across every platform adapter. Not fixed this cycle: no ground-truth corpus exists to measure the false-negative cost of (a), and shipping an unvalidated semantic change to an identity-fusion rule violates the priority ladder more than the known FP does.
